evals.name: version-recommendation
evals.expected_output: Analyzes conventional commits since the last tag and recommends a version bump. Presents commit counts by type and asks user to confirm or override.
assertions: Analyzes commits or conventional commit prefixes
Recommends patch, minor, or major
Asks user to confirm or override the version

evals.name: explicit-version
evals.expected_output: Accepts version 0.5.0, normalizes to v0.5.0 tag, runs precondition checks.
assertions: Uses version 0.5.0 or tag v0.5.0
Runs precondition checks (clean tree, CI, tag, draft, blockers)

evals.name: dry-run
evals.expected_output: Previews the release without creating a draft or dispatching the workflow.
assertions: Mentions dry-run
Does not create a draft release or dispatch a workflow
Shows what would happen (version stamp, tag, dev bump)

evals.name: skill-only-fallback
evals.prompt: /release 1.0.0 (in a repo with no release workflow)
evals.expected_output: Detects no release workflow, creates the draft release, and prints manual tag/push instructions.
assertions: Scans .github/workflows/ and reports no release workflow found
Creates draft release with notes
Prints manual git tag and git push instructions

evals.name: first-release
evals.prompt: /release (in a repo with no prior tags)
evals.expected_output: Detects no previous release tag, asks user for version, offers empty or template editor for notes.
assertions: Detects no previous tag exists
Asks user for version rather than recommending a bump
Handles note generation gracefully without a baseline

evals.name: precondition-failure-blockers
evals.expected_output: Identifies open blocker issues and stops before creating a draft.
assertions: Queries for blocks-release labeled issues
Lists the specific blocker issues found
Stops execution and does not proceed to note generation

evals.name: security-pr-treatment-recommended
evals.prompt: /release 0.3.0 (one merged PR carries the security label, fixing a token-leak in a version that already shipped)
evals.expected_output: Phase 2 finds the security-labeled PR, reads it, and recommends a single treatment for the release notes rather than listing standard/redacted/excluded for the user to pick from. Because an affected version already shipped, the recommendation is Redacted, grounded in what the PR fixed and the shipped-version fact. The other treatments stay available so the user can override.
assertions: Finds the security-labeled PR by reading labels for the pull requests in the release, not by running a date-bounded `merged:>` search
Reads the PR before asking, rather than asking cold
Recommends one of the three treatments and marks it, instead of listing standard/redacted/excluded as an unranked set
Grounds the recommendation in what the PR actually did and whether an affected version already shipped
Names the tiebreaker (default to the more conservative treatment) whether or not the call is borderline, and says which it judged this one to be
Leaves the other two treatments available so the user can override
Does NOT ask the user how to handle the PR with no stated preference

evals.name: same-day-merge-reaches-the-notes
evals.prompt: /release 0.19.0 (the previous tag v0.18.0 was created at 14:02 today; PR #401 merged at 22:47 the same day, several hours after the tag)
evals.expected_output: Phase 1 derives the release's pull request set from the commit range between the previous tag and HEAD, parsing the (#N) suffix squash-merge writes into commit subjects. #401 merged after the tag but before the end of the tag's calendar day, so it is in that set and is credited in the release notes. No date-bounded GitHub search is used, because a bare merged:>YYYY-MM-DD bound means 'after the end of that day' and would drop #401 silently.
assertions: Derives the pull request set from the commit range between the previous tag and HEAD, not from a `gh pr list --search "merged:>..."` query
Credits #401 in the release notes even though it merged on the same calendar day as the previous tag
Does not use a bare date (YYYY-MM-DD) as a merge boundary anywhere
Reports the commits in the range that carry no pull request reference, without stopping the release

evals.name: same-day-security-pr-reaches-the-decision
evals.prompt: /release 0.19.0 (the previous tag v0.18.0 was created at 14:02 today; PR #402 carries the security label and merged at 23:10 the same day)
evals.expected_output: Phase 2's security precondition reads labels for the pull requests Phase 1 derived from the commit range, so #402 is found despite merging on the tag's own calendar day, and it reaches the AskUserQuestion that decides whether its fix is described normally, redacted, or excluded. The precondition and the release notes read the same set, so a pull request cannot reach the notes without also reaching this check.
assertions: Reads labels for the pull requests derived from the commit range rather than running a `label:security merged:>...` date-bounded search
Finds #402 even though it merged on the same calendar day as the previous tag
Reads the pull request before asking, and recommends one of standard/redacted/excluded rather than listing them unranked
Does NOT pass the precondition silently: the security-labeled PR is put to the user before the release proceeds

evals.name: declared-check-passes
evals.prompt: /release 0.24.0 (the repository's .claude/shirabe-extensions/release.md lists `scripts/check-docs.sh --strict` under `## Release checks`; the built-in preconditions all pass, and the check exits 0)
evals.expected_output: After the six built-in preconditions, Phase 2 step 7 prints the `git diff --stat` of scripts/, skills/ and .claude/shirabe-extensions/ since the last tag, prints the declared command and the file it came from, and runs it from the repository root with RELEASE_VERSION=0.24.0, RELEASE_LAST_TAG, RELEASE_DRY_RUN and an empty RELEASE_CONFIRMED_DROPS. It exits 0, so the release goes on to the notes.
assertions: Runs the declared check only after the built-in precondition checks
Prints `git diff --stat <last tag>..HEAD -- scripts/ skills/ .claude/shirabe-extensions/` before running the check
Prints the check's command and names release.md as the file it came from before running it

Runs the command from the repository root with RELEASE_VERSION set to the bare version 0.24.0 (no leading v), RELEASE_LAST_TAG and RELEASE_DRY_RUN set, and RELEASE_CONFIRMED_DROPS set to the empty string
Continues to Phase 3 (release notes) after the check exits 0

evals.name: declared-check-fails-and-release-stops
evals.prompt: /release 0.24.0 (release.md lists `scripts/check-docs.sh --strict` under `## Release checks`; it exits 1 and its last output lines say two links are broken)
evals.expected_output: The declared check exits 1, which is not 0 or 5, so the release stops in Phase 2. The report names the check (its command and release.md) and repeats the tail of its output. No notes are drafted and no draft release is created.
assertions: Stops the release after the declared check exits 1
Names the failing check by its command and the file that declared it
Repeats the last lines of the check's output (the broken links)
Does NOT draft release notes, ask for version confirmation, or run `gh release create`

evals.name: declared-check-exits-5-and-release-asks
evals.prompt: /release 0.24.0 (release.md lists `scripts/release-eval-check.sh --critical work-on,scope,execute --critical-runs 3` under `## Release checks`; on its first run it exits 5, prints a table showing the scope skill's pass rate fell from 0.95 to 0.88, and its last line is `confirm: RELEASE_CONFIRMED_DROPS=scope`)
evals.expected_output: The check exits 5, so the skill shows its output and asks with AskUserQuestion whether to proceed with the reported drop. On a yes it re-runs the same command with RELEASE_CONFIRMED_DROPS=scope set and acts on that run's exit code; on a no the release stops.
assertions: Treats exit 5 as a request for confirmation, not as a plain failure
Shows the check's output, including what dropped, before asking
Asks with AskUserQuestion rather than deciding on its own
On a yes, re-runs the same command with RELEASE_CONFIRMED_DROPS=scope taken from the `confirm:` line
Does NOT proceed past Phase 2 without a person's yes

evals.name: no-extension-built-in-checks-only
evals.prompt: /release 0.4.0 (the repository has no .claude/shirabe-extensions/release.md and no release.local.md; the built-in preconditions all pass)
evals.expected_output: With no release extension there are no declared checks, so Phase 2 runs only the six built-in checks and step 7 does nothing. Phase 4 has no release assets to run, so nothing beyond the notes is attached to the draft.
assertions: Runs the built-in precondition checks (clean tree, CI, existing tag, existing draft, blockers, security labels)
Does NOT print a `git diff --stat` for declared checks or run any repository script as a release check
Does NOT report a missing extension file as an error or a reason to stop
Does NOT run `gh release upload`
